decision: WF-097 threshold boundary: a published quote whose activity count exactly equals the configured high-activity threshold is classified Low activity (count <= threshold is Low) or High activity (only count < threshold is Low, so count == threshold is High).

state.sourced_sentence_1: Settings > Objects > Quotes > 'Analyze quote activity level tracking threshold': enter the high activity threshold. 'Published quotes with activity below this threshold are classified as Low activity.'
state.sourced_sentence_2: In the 'Your published quotes' bubble chart, 'quotes below the threshold render black and above it green; hover for name, expiration date and activity count'.
state.what_is_at_stake: One comparison in one pure rule, plus the colour a bubble chart point and a status chip get. The count compared is the Activity Count on the quote object, and the threshold is a workspace setting a super admin sets.
state.why_it_is_ambiguous: Both sourced sentences use the same two words, below and above, and neither names the equality case. Sentence 1 says below is Low and is silent about equal. Sentence 2 says below is black and above is green and is also silent about equal. Reading below as strictly less than makes equality High in sentence 1 and unclassified in sentence 2. Reading below as at or below makes equality Low in both, which contradicts sentence 2's 'above it green' only if above is read as inclusive.
state.note: No other sentence in the researched specification mentions the comparison. The setting is per workspace and editable by a super admin.

options.below_is_low_equal_is_high: Only a count strictly below the threshold is Low activity. A count equal to the threshold is High activity. This follows sentence 1 on its plain reading, where 'below this threshold' excludes equality. It treats the threshold as the minimum count that qualifies as high.
options.at_or_below_is_low: A count at or below the threshold is Low activity and only a count strictly above it is High. This follows the bubble-chart sentence on its plain reading, where 'below the threshold render black and above it green' leaves the threshold point itself on the low side. It treats the threshold as the highest count that still counts as low.
options.unconfigured_and_equal_both_unclassified: A count equal to the threshold is reported as neither Low nor High and is rendered with a distinct label, because neither sentence covers it. The page says the threshold comparison is ambiguous for this quote. This adds a third class the researched vocabulary does not name.

reason: chose 'below_is_low_equal_is_high' but confidence 0.45 < 0.75; insufficient evidence to gate on

criteria.below_is_low_equal_is_high: Implement count < threshold as Low activity and count >= threshold as High activity.
criteria.at_or_below_is_low: Implement count <= threshold as Low activity and count > threshold as High activity.
criteria.unconfigured_and_equal_both_unclassified: Add a third class for the equality case rather than picking a side.

state.sourced_sentence_1: Settings > Objects > Quotes, field named 'Analyze quote activity level tracking threshold', help text: 'Published quotes with activity below this threshold are classified as Low activity.'
state.sourced_sentence_2: In the 'Your published quotes' bubble chart, 'quotes below the threshold render black and above it green; hover for name, expiration date and activity count'.
state.codebase_precedent: Two shipped features in this repository compare a count with a threshold and both use strict greater-than: dsr/crm_backfill/plan.py says 'more than the threshold asks for an async job; at or below it, a paged read', and dsr/change_stream/gap_vocabulary.py says a change count above the researched threshold overflows. state.rendered_outcome_for_a_concrete_case: A super admin sets the threshold to 10. A published quote has an Activity Count of exactly 10. Under the at-or-below reading the quote renders as Low activity and its chart point renders black. Under the below-only reading it renders as High activity and its chart point renders green.
state.what_the_setting_is_for: The setting lives under an Analyse heading in the Quotes object settings. Its purpose is to separate a quote a buyer is actively working on from one the buyer has abandoned. The number a person types is the count at which they have decided a quote counts as engaged.
state.cost_of_at_or_below: A super admin who types 10 has said that 10 activities is the engagement level, and the page then tells them a quote with 10 activities is Low activity. The only way to make that quote green is to raise the setting to 9. Every seller who reads the chart has to reverse-engineer the boundary, and the follow-up list would offer a follow up on a quote at exactly the engagement level the workspace set as its bar.
state.cost_of_below_only: A quote at exactly the threshold is green, which is one more activity than the prose strictly requires. No other sentence in the specification depends on the equality case, so nothing else in the product observes the difference.
state.why_the_prose_is_still_ambiguous: The word below in both sentences is strict English for less than. Sentence 1 names Low activity as what is below the threshold, so equality is not below and not Low. Sentence 2 says below is black and above is green, which leaves the point on the threshold itself uncoloured, so it does not contradict sentence 1 read strictly.

state.the_four_counters: Last Activity Date, Activity Count, Activity Count Since Last Communication, View Count. All four are index-page columns on the quote object.
state.sourced_sentence_1: Data sources include 'connected email channel (for "since last communication")'.
state.sourced_sentence_2: Index page: read the Last Activity Date, Activity Count, Activity Count Since Last Communication and View Count columns.

state.product_fact: This product has no mail transport. A sibling workflow on this repository states in its own docstring that no message is transmitted and that the recorded send event is the record. No workflow provisions an email channel, and this workflow may not edit shared files to add one.
state.what_this_workflow_records: Every event it writes is either an outbound action by the seller or a buyer interaction with the hosted quote. It records no inbound email reply, so it cannot observe a buyer answering.
state.rendered_outcome_for_a_concrete_case: A published quote was sent to the buyer nine days ago and the buyer has not replied. The last event in the activity log is that send, nine days old.
state.cost_of_reporting_a_number: The column would read 9. The buyer may well have answered by email nine days ago and the seller never saw it. The page would tell a seller that the buyer has been silent for nine days when the buyer has been silent for none. That number drives the follow-up recommendation, so a wrong number here produces a follow up that a seller should not have sent.
state.cost_of_reporting_unavailable: In this build the column reads 'No email channel connected' on every quote. Three of the four columns work. The follow-up rules still run on last activity date and on the expiration date, so no recommendation is lost. The column is not a dead control: it states the fact that the product cannot support the figure, and it becomes a number as soon as a workspace records a channel.
state.why_the_prose_is_still_ambiguous: The research names the channel as the source for this one column and says nothing about the column when no channel is connected.
state.verification: Whatever is chosen is recorded in the domain module beside the rule it governs, with the rejected option and the cost of rejecting it, and served on the vocabulary route so a reviewer can read it.
